title: new accepts a repro whose own shell -c string misses a tool after its first command, read as a wrapper's inside tool
goal: own_failure reads every command word of a shell -c string (split on &&, ||, ; and |) as the repro's own, so a not-found message naming any of them is the repro's own error (cannot start), and only a name in none of them counts as a tool inside a wrapper; a test plants sh -c 'cd /tmp && jq .' and bash -c 'ls | jqx .' with exit 127 and both are refused, while bash hook.sh naming jq stays accepted. Found by the SP-xdzgepun review of BG-a3ubazze.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_land as b;sys.exit(0 if b.own_failure(['sh','-c','cd /tmp && jq .'],127,'sh: line 1: jq: command not found','.') else 1)
